problem:
Original unrestricted S02, unchanged, as context and conventions:
Let X=(C^3 minus {0})/<z maps to exp(-1) z> be the standard compact Hopf threefold. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi)) partial barpartial and d^c=(i/(4 pi))(barpartial-partial). On its cover put s=log|z|^2, alpha=dd^c s, beta=ds wedge d^c s and omega=alpha+beta. These forms descend, omega is positive Hermitian, alpha=pi^*omega_FS for the projectivization pi:X->CP^2, int_CP2 omega_FS^2=1, dd^c beta=-alpha^2, dd^c omega^2=0 and int_X omega^3=6. The elliptic fibers are E=C/(Z+2 pi i Z), with probability Haar area dA_E=(i/(4 pi))dw wedge dbarw. For every smooth real v the exact mass identity is int_X(omega+dd^c v)^3=6+6 int_CP2 (int_pi^-1(y)|partial_w v|^2 dA_E)omega_FS^2(y). Positivity is not assumed in this algebraic identity.

A normalized omega-psh potential u is a genuine quasi-plurisubharmonic function with its canonical upper representative, with omega+dd^c u>=0 as a current and sup_X u=0. Locally quasi-plurisubharmonic means a genuine plurisubharmonic function plus a smooth real function; arbitrary upward pointwise modifications are excluded. Define its extended non-pluripolar measure mu_u=MA_ext_omega(u) by the increasing compatible measures 1_{u>-k}(omega+dd^c max(u,-k))^3; the product for bounded quasi-psh functions is the local Bedford--Taylor expansion against the smooth background. The pole set has measure zero, and total mass is allowed to be infinite. Cap_omega(A)=sup{int_A(omega+dd^c v)^3: v is omega-psh, -1<=v<=0}. Capacity convergence means Cap_omega({|u_j-u|>delta})->0 for every delta>0, with the usual extended-value interpretation.

Let W:[0,infinity)->(0,infinity) be continuously differentiable and nonincreasing, with W(t)->0. Set nu_W,u=W(-u)mu_u, assigning weight zero on the pole set. Determine sharp decay conditions on W for (i) finiteness of nu_W,u for every normalized u, (ii) a uniform total-mass bound over all normalized u, (iii) uniform tails sup_u nu_W,u({-u>T})->0, (iv) uniform absolute continuity with respect to Cap_omega and weak continuity u_j->u in capacity implies nu_W,u_j->nu_W,u. Separate these properties if their thresholds differ. State exactly what is proved for general decreasing weights and for the power/logarithmic families.

Known background: BMP fails by the smooth Xia--Zhang Hopf counterexample, arXiv:2608.21053v1; its primary source uses dd^c=i partial barpartial, so normalization must be converted if used. The known restricted-depth bound is mu_u({u>=-T})<=C(1+T), and mu_u(A intersect {u>=-T})<=(1+T)^3 Cap_omega(A). The general damping theorem therefore gives all four properties when int_0^infinity(1+t)(-W'(t))dt<infinity. In particular W(t)=(1+t)^-1[log(e+t)]^-a works for a>1, as do stronger powers and exponential weights. These are existing sufficient bounds, not a solution of the optimal-rate question. No candidate construction, new scale, proof or sharpness argument is supplied.

Proposed restricted targets, all require proof:
# Proposed S02 rotational-sector conclusions; all require proof

Keep every convention and measure/capacity definition of original S02.
Let R be the ENTIRE class of normalized genuine omega-psh potentials on the
standard scalar Hopf threefold invariant under (z0,z')->(z0,A z'), A in U(2).
Include bounded and unbounded potentials. No reduction of arbitrary potentials
to R is granted. W is positive C1, nonincreasing and tends to zero. Put
Q(W)=sup_(t>=0)(1+sqrt(2t))W(t) and
Q_T(W)=sup_(t>=T)(1+sqrt(2t))W(t).

A. Every individual nu_W,u for u in R is finite if and only if
sup_(t large) sqrt(t)W(t)<infinity. The same condition is equivalent to
a uniform total-mass bound on R. Prove the actual quantitative upper bound
sup_R nu_W,u(X)<=12 Q(W). If the condition fails, construct ONE actual
genuine normalized invariant potential with infinite weighted measure;
unbounded masses of a sequence alone do not establish this conclusion.

B. Uniform tails on R hold exactly when sqrt(t)W(t)->0. Prove for every
actual bounded or unbounded u in R and every T>=0 the bound
nu_W,u({-u>T})<=12 Q_T(W), with extended interpretation if the bound is
infinite. When the limiting condition fails, give actual admissible
potentials and actual deep-set mass that prevents uniform tail decay.

C. Uniform absolute continuity relative to the ORIGINAL Cap_omega holds
on R exactly when sqrt(t)W(t)->0. Prove the quantitative bound, for every
Borel A and T>=0,
nu_W,u(A)<=W(0)(1+T)^3 Cap_omega(A)+12 Q_T(W).
Construct actual small-capacity sets carrying uniformly positive weighted
mass whenever limsup sqrt(t)W(t)>0; unrelated measures are not a substitute.

D. The map from all of R into finite measures is continuous from original
capacity convergence to weak convergence exactly when sqrt(t)W(t)->0.
When sqrt(t)W(t) is bounded but does not tend to zero, construct an ACTUAL
smooth normalized invariant sequence u_j converging in original capacity
to an ACTUAL genuine normalized invariant g, for which weighted measures
have a finite weak cluster carrying positive mass on an analytic pole
divisor of g while nu_W,g has zero mass there. Prove every product and
capacity limit, including bounded-truncation mass on depth level sets.
When sqrt(t)W(t) is unbounded, A already obstructs a map into finite
measures on all R; do not relabel this as a finite weak-limit example.

E. For eventually decreasing weights (1+t)^(-p)log(e+t)^(-a) tending to
zero, modified smoothly on a compact interval if needed, individual
finiteness and uniform total bounds hold on R exactly for p>1/2 or
p=1/2,a>=0; tails, capacity absolute continuity and capacity-to-weak
continuity hold exactly for p>1/2 or p=1/2,a>0. All necessary obstructions
also apply to the unrestricted original class, but the sufficient
conclusions above are for R ONLY. Original S02 remains incomplete.

Independently reconstruct all A--E and their entire dependency chain,
verifying exact indispensable primary hypotheses, global positivity,
canonical normalization and pole values, actual measures and every limit.
No author proof, prior report or source-application judgment is supplied.
These are proposed theorem conclusions rather than granted lemmas.


PRECISELY PERMITTED PRIMARY-ASSESSED FOUNDATIONS, NOT TARGET CONCLUSIONS:
On the scalar Hopf threefold, with dd^c_src=i partial barpartial and omega_src=i partial barpartial s+i partial s wedge barpartial s, s=log|z|^2, put xi=z'/z0, w=log z0, x=log|xi|^2 and mu=e^x/(1+e^x). For smooth real V(x,w), its local Hermitian matrix in the alpha_src-unit tangential, alpha_src-unit radial and partial/partial w frame is [[(mu+V_x)/mu,0,0],[0,(mu+V_xx)/(mu(1-mu)),(mu+V_xbarw)/sqrt(mu(1-mu))],[0,(mu+V_wx)/sqrt(mu(1-mu)),1+V_wbarw]]. If V is independent of x for sufficiently negative x and constant in x,w for sufficiently positive x, it extends smoothly globally; positivity at xi=0 is equivalent to 1+V_wbarw>0. Xia--Zhang, Lemma2.2, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.21053v1. Both the source operator and background must be divided by2pi, leaving the scalar potential unchanged. The endpoint extension hypothesis is not asserted for every smooth member of R.
For E=C/(Z+2pi i Z), probability Haar area dA=i dw wedge dbarw/(4pi), k_t(w)=(2/t) sum_lambda exp(-|w-lambda|^2/t), and F_eta(t,w)=-eta int_t^infinity(k_r(w)-1)dr, 0<eta<1/10, one has F_eta,t=F_eta,wbarw=eta(k_t-1), (log k_t)_wbarw>=-1/t, and ||partial_t^a F_eta(t,.)||_C^m<=C_a,m eta exp(-t/4) for t>=1 and fixed nonnegative integers a,m, uniformly in eta. Xia--Zhang, Lemma3.1, at the same primary URL.
For that k_t, absolute constants C0>=1 and C exist such that t k_t<=C0 exp(-|t partial_barw log k_t|^2/(C0t)) for0<t<=1. If0<kappa<1/(200C0),0<eta<1/10,0<t<=1,1/2<=mu<=1, sigma=sqrt((2kappa/eta)log(1/(eta t))), h=eta k_t and zeta=(sigma/mu)t partial_barw log k_t, then kappa t k_t-mu^2(1-eta)h|zeta-(1-eta)^(-1)|^2/(1-eta+h)<=C kappa exp(-1/(C sigma^2 t)), uniformly in all these parameters and w. Xia--Zhang, Lemmas3.2--3.3, at the same primary URL. No faster heat scale, global correction, core mass or limiting counterexample is granted.
For Omega contained in C^n and locally bounded genuine psh p1,...,pk, k<=n, their Bedford--Taylor mixed product is a positive closed current, local and symmetric multilinear in its arguments, and weakly continuous under simultaneous decreasing locally bounded psh limits. Bedford--Taylor, Theorem2.1 and Corollary2.2, https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf. Their dd^c_src=2i partial barpartial equals4pi times the present operator, so actual products and local capacity constants must be rescaled.
For locally bounded psh p,q on Omega contained in C^n and compactly supported smooth (n-k,n-k)-forms phi,1<=k<=n, int phi[(dd^c p)^k-(dd^c q)^k]=sum_(l=0)^(k-1) int(p-q)dd^c phi wedge(dd^c p)^l wedge(dd^c q)^(k-1-l). This is Bedford--Taylor Corollary2.8 and its mixed-degree integration-by-parts consequence; no integration by parts with a falsely closed Hermitian background is granted.
For K compactly contained in Omega contained in C^n, bounded psh p1,...,pk,k<=n, and the Euclidean Kahler form beta, int_K dd^c p1 wedge...wedge dd^c pk wedge beta^(n-k)<=C_(K,Omega,k) product_i ||pi||_L^infinity(Omega). Bedford--Taylor, Theorem2.10. Its complete printed statement is permitted; that source cites the estimates rather than giving their proof there. No recursive certification of every cited foundation is claimed.
On a bounded domain Omega contained in C^n, every genuine psh function is quasi-continuous for relative Bedford--Taylor capacity: for each epsilon>0 there is an open O contained in Omega with C(O,Omega)<epsilon such that its restriction to Omega minus O is continuous. Bedford--Taylor, Theorem3.5. The present argument needs this only for locally bounded corrected psh functions on relatively compact coordinate balls.
On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain Omega contained in C^n, every locally pluripolar set has zero outer Bedford--Taylor capacity. Bedford--Taylor, Theorem6.9. No unproved equivalence with the present global Hermitian capacity is granted.
On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex Omega contained in C^n, if compact subsets K_j decrease to K, then C(K_j,Omega) decreases to C(K,Omega); also C*(K,Omega)=C(K,Omega). Bedford--Taylor, Proposition6.4.
On an open Omega contained in C^n, a decreasing sequence of genuine psh functions has a genuine locally integrable psh pointwise limit whenever the limit is not identically minus infinity on any component. A distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine psh representative. The cone Psh(Omega) intersect L1_loc(Omega) is closed in L1_loc, and its L1_loc-bounded subsets are relatively compact. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry,I.4.17,I.5.4 andI.5.8--5.9, https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf. The canonical distributional current and the genuine upper representative are essential. The statement ofI.5.9 is permitted; its inherited subharmonic compactness foundations are not recursively certified here.
The original task's increasing compatible non-pluripolar truncation measures, pole-set mass zero, normalization and restricted-depth capacity bound are permitted exactly as originally stated. If used as an indexed premise in the report, state that mathematical foundation separately and bind it to its exact matching original grant, rather than attaching its quote to an unrelated external theorem.
Elementary local submean inequalities, compact connected chart-cover propagation of a common L1 bound, finite-dimensional Hermitian matrix algebra, compact-group Haar averaging, measure-theoretic monotone convergence, Portmanteau, finite-measure compactness on a compact space, and continuous extension from a closed subset are permitted foundations. No positive-flux identity, semiconvex depth bound, rotational weighted estimate, capacity comparison, symmetry smoothing, bounded nonclosed weighted convergence, critical concentration or original-task completion is granted.
